pages.text: Pour liquid concrete from a bucket into a mould of any shape: the liquid turns into $(item)concrete$() blocks on its own. This is the easiest way to cast walls and floors without crafting.

$(l)Shapes$()$(br)In a stonecutter, one concrete block gives:$(li)$(item)2 concrete slabs$(), or stairs, or a wall,$(li)$(item)8 cinderblocks$(), the small grey bricks.$(br2)Six cinderblocks around two rebar and a bucket of liquid concrete craft $(item)8 cinder blocks$(), the full-size wall block.

$(l)Colours$()$(br)Surround a dye with $(item)8 concrete$() in a crafting grid to get 8 coloured concrete. All sixteen colours exist, each with its own slab, stairs and wall from the stonecutter. Rebar concrete is dyed the same way.

$(l)Smokestacks$()$(br)Concrete with industrial pipes also crafts the $(item)concrete smokestack$() used to vent CO2.$(br2)For pillars, floors and the most industrial look, use rebar concrete, explained on the next page. It comes in the same sixteen colours.
